equipment_description: name: Atomic Absorption Spectrometer (AAS) [SEP] aliases: AAS; atomic absorption [SEP] short description: Atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS) is an elemental analysis method for determining the concentration of metals in a given sample. The principle of AAS relies on the vaporization of metals within a sample when introduced to a flame. Every ground state metal absorbs light radiation (and excites) at a different wavelength. Equipment at University of Cambridge. [SEP] typical applications: Double, slit photoelectron interference in strong, field ionization of the neon dimer (Nature Communications, 2018), TheGaiamission (Astronomy and Astrophysics, 2016), Stochastic resonance (Reviews of Modern Physics, 1998), The formation, properties and impact of secondary organic aerosol: current and emerging issues (Atmospheric chemistry and physics, 2009), New handbook for standardised measurement of plant functional traits worldwide (Australian Journal of Botany, 2013) [SEP] tags: AAS, elemental analysis, flame

equipment_description: name: Auger Electron Spectrometer (AES) [SEP] aliases: AES; Auger spectroscopy [SEP] short description: Auger electron spectroscopy (AES; pronounced [oʒe] in French) is a common analytical technique used specifically in the study of surfaces and, more generally, in the area of materials science. It is a form of electron spectroscopy that relies on the Auger effect, based on the analysis of energetic electrons emitted from an excited atom after a series of internal relaxation events. The Auger effect was discovered independently by both Lise Meitner and Pierre Auger in the 1920s. Equipment at University of Portsmouth. [SEP] typical applications: Femtosecond X, ray protein nanocrystallography (Nature, 2011), Fundamentals and advances in magnesium alloy corrosion (Progress in Materials Science, 2017), Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector (The Astrophysical Journal, 1998), Low, threshold amplified spontaneous emission and lasing from colloidal nanocrystals of caesium lead halide perovskites (Nature Communications, 2015), Electron, Ion Collider: The next QCD frontier (The European Physical Journal A, 2016) [SEP] tags: Auger, surface analysis, elemental
